evidence_packet.summary: Lieutenant Fred Naylor, of Aspull, and Company Sgt Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, died in 1918
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in March and April 1918 and were both named on memorials to the missing Naylor was first identified as "unknown soldier" by badges on his uniform, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) said Ministry of Defence (MOD) case worker Alexia Clark said: "Working on cases where there is a chance to reunite a man with his name is always special." The research was carried out by the MOD, the National Army Museum and CWGC CWGC case worker Polly Brewster said: "We are honoured to have played a role in the identification of their final resting places."

evidence_packet.summary: Kyle Howard, 37, of Rochdale, killed Keeley Aspinall in "a devastating act of domestic abuse", police say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who murdered his wife and hid her body under their bed has been jailed Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Howard was sentenced to a minimum of 21-and-a-half years in prison at Manchester Crown Court, after earlier pleading guilty to murder In a victim impact statement read to the court, Keeley's sister said: "I have never been so heartbroken in my life. I just wish I could have one more second with my sister." "I miss her so much and I'll never get to see her again," her sister said. title: Six more arrests in Crumpsall murder investigation over stab death

evidence_packet.title: Six more arrests in Crumpsall murder investigation over stab death
evidence_packet.lead: Seven people are now in custody over the death of a 27-year-old man in north Manchester
evidence_packet.summary: Seven people are now in custody over the death of a 27-year-old man in north Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Six more arrests in Crumpsall murder investigation over stab death - BBC News Image caption, A 27-year-old man was stabbed to death in Crumpsall on Saturday By Marc Waddington North West Published 18 November 2026 Six more people have been arrested as part of a murder probe launched after a man was stabbed to death. A 27-year-old man died in Moss Bank in Crumpsall, Manchester, shortly after 01:30 GMT on Saturday, following an attack by "a number of males". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said it had arrested two men on suspicion of murder, and four other people on suspicion of assisting an offender. Another man arrested after the incident on suspicion of murder, remains in custody, the force said. The victim was reported to have been set upon by a number of men wearing balaclavas. Of the seven people held as part of the investigation, two are men, aged 24 and 25, who are being questioned on suspicion of murder. Two men, aged 33 and 35, and two women, aged 21 and 34, are being questioned on suspicion of assisting an offender. The other murder suspect is a 26-year-old man, the force said. Det Insp Neil Higginson said: "Our investigation is continuing at a pace and we now have six more people in our custody. "Even though we have made seven arrests in total, we are continuing to investigate this tragic death and are appealing for the public to assist us. "I would still urge anyone who witnessed the incident, saw the movements of vehicles, or has any information that could assist our investigation to contact us however insignificant you think it might be." Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone. And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said. The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly. Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference. "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said. Deputy Mayor Kate Green said: "They are not speed cameras, they are being used for crime detection and as an investigative tool." title: Graves of missing North West soldiers found in Belgium and France

evidence_packet.title: Graves of missing North West soldiers found in Belgium and France
evidence_packet.lead: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in M
evidence_packet.summary: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in M
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The graves of two lost World War One soldiers from the north-west of England have been found in Belgium and France more than a century after their deaths Lieutenant Fred Naylor from Aspull, in Wigan, and Company Sergeant Major Herbert Bannister, of Wavertree, Liverpool, died in March and April 1918 and were both named on memorials to the missing Naylor was first identified as "unknown soldier" by badges on his uniform, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) said Ministry of Defence (MOD) case worker Alexia Clark said: "Working on cases where there is a chance to reunite a man with his name is always special." The research was carried out by the MOD, the National Army Museum and CWGC CWGC case worker Polly Brewster said: "We are honoured to have played a role in the identification of their final resting places."

evidence_packet.summary: A woman who survived the Dambusters raid during World War Two has climbed into the cockpit of a replica Lancaster bomber used in the famous mission Christa Chadwick was nine when RAF 617 Squadron flew over Germany's Ruhr Valley in an operation to breach three dams on the night of
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who survived the Dambusters raid during World War Two has climbed into the cockpit of a replica Lancaster bomber used in the famous mission Christa Chadwick was nine when RAF 617 Squadron flew over Germany's Ruhr Valley in an operation to breach three dams on the night of 16 and 17 May 1943 She recalled: "People were running around through the streets screaming, 'Das wasser kommt' [the water is coming] Chadwick, from Knutsford, Cheshire, stepped inside a replica of a bomber during a visit to the Avro Heritage Museum in Woodford, Stockport The museum is located at the site of the former Woodford Aerodrome where famous aircraft, including the Lancaster bomber, were built About 1,300 people were killed in the flooding that followed the bombing of Möhne dam and the Eder dam

title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest

evidence_packet.title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest
evidence_packet.lead: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was fi
evidence_packet.summary: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was fi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017

title: Government 'determined' to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader

evidence_packet.title: Government 'determined' to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader
evidence_packet.lead: The government is still considering "every option" to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed, a Home Office minister has said, months after ministers suggested emergency legislation could be used to remove him from the UK Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July aft
evidence_packet.summary: The government is still considering "every option" to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed, a Home Office minister has said, months after ministers suggested emergency legislation could be used to remove him from the UK Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July aft
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government is still considering "every option" to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed, a Home Office minister has said, months after ministers suggested emergency legislation could be used to remove him from the UK Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after serving 14 years for rape and other sexual offences against girls, some as young as 12 The government said at the time that it would seek to deport Ahmed to Pakistan. Having been stripped of his British citizenship, he now holds only Pakistani nationality However, he remains in the UK because existing legislation prevents the deportation of some Commonwealth citizens A minister said earlier that officials were "determined" to remove him from the country Lord Collins of Highbury was asked in the House of Lords whether the Home Office had threatened Pakistan with the withdrawal of foreign aid or visa sanctions

title: Rochdale man who murdered wife and hid body under bed jailed

evidence_packet.title: Rochdale man who murdered wife and hid body under bed jailed
evidence_packet.lead: A man who murdered his wife and hid her body under their bed has been jailed Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said
evidence_packet.summary: A man who murdered his wife and hid her body under their bed has been jailed Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who murdered his wife and hid her body under their bed has been jailed Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Howard was sentenced to a minimum of 21-and-a-half years in prison at Manchester Crown Court, after earlier pleading guilty to murder In a victim impact statement read to the court, Keeley's sister said: "I have never been so heartbroken in my life. I just wish I could have one more second with my sister." "I miss her so much and I'll never get to see her again," her sister said. "That was his choice to take her away "I have nightmares about what has happened to her - but I have found that being awake is worse than the actual nightmares I have at night."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former chief executive of a non-league football club who plotted to drug and rape a man's wife has pleaded guilty to separate child abuse image offences Karl Lindsay, who stepped down from his post at Taunton Town in Somerset last year, last month admitted charges of conspiracy to rape and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent to stupefy The 56-year-old had pleaded guilty shortly before he was due to go on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court alongside nine other men who deny their alleged roles in the abuse of the wife in Stockport He appeared at the same court earlier by prison videolink and entered more guilty pleas to offences not connected with the ongoing trial Lindsay, of Taunton, admitted three offences of making indecent images of children between February 2024 and November 2025 He made 10 still images and eight moving images classed as category A, the most serious, two moving class B images, and 11 still class C images

title: Police now using scrapped Clean Air Zone cameras to catch criminals

evidence_packet.title: Police now using scrapped Clean Air Zone cameras to catch criminals
evidence_packet.lead: Police have been catching criminals by using cameras installed as part of an abandoned Clean Air Zone scheme Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wid
evidence_packet.summary: Police have been catching criminals by using cameras installed as part of an abandoned Clean Air Zone scheme Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wid
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police have been catching criminals by using cameras installed as part of an abandoned Clean Air Zone scheme Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said

evidence_packet.summary: A mystery medal belonging to a soldier who was killed in World War One is set to be handed over to his family Joyce Smith found the medal, assigned to Private Joseph Newbury, from The Sherwood Foresters (Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire Regiment), among her late husband's collectio
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mystery medal belonging to a soldier who was killed in World War One is set to be handed over to his family Joyce Smith found the medal, assigned to Private Joseph Newbury, from The Sherwood Foresters (Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire Regiment), among her late husband's collection at her home in Bolton and appealed for help to find relatives of the soldier Historian Andy Bye got in touch and tracked down the great granddaughters of Pte Newbury, from Derby, after finding his military records The granddaughters are now planning to meet Smith who will give them medal to keep Amanda Reed, 60, from Bramhall in Greater Manchester, said it was kind of Bye to carry out the research into her great grandfather, who died in September 1915 "What a lovely thing of Andy to do, to go to all that trouble, to find the family, basically, of people that he doesn't even know," she said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel" The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning" A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites" Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers

title: Health warning issued as forecasters predict snow in North West

evidence_packet.title: Health warning issued as forecasters predict snow in North West
evidence_packet.lead: NHS leaders in the north-west of England have urged people to take steps to protect their health as forecasters warn of snow A yellow warning for wintry weather in Greater Manchester and Lancashire came into force at midnight and will apply until 11:00 GMT Meanwhile the UK Health

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The secrets that led to the downfall of five prison officers The Prison Service in England and Wales have developed a scheme given to trainees to help them avoid being manipulated into illicit relationships by experienced criminals Top row, lef Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:01, 19 Nov 2026 Updated 07:42, 19 Nov 2026 It's a position held in the highest regard with the intense responsibility of guarding the most violent in our society. With that responsibility comes great scrutiny However, for some, temptation proved too much. In March 2026, the Ministry of Justice stated that between 2020 and 2025, 41 prison officers had been convicted of an offence of misconduct in a public office , where the offence related to an inappropriate relationship with a prison The Prison Service has since developed a scheme, the Enable programme, which designed to assist trainees with professional practice, capability and strengthening learning It is currently piloting a regional delivery model across London prisons and testing the model in Early Adopter sites, the service said. A redesigned Foundation Training programme for new prison officers is also being developed, with testing due to begin in 2027 A Prison Service spokesperson said: “Prison officers are the backbone of our service, working every day in some of the toughest conditions. That is why getting training right is essential to delivering punishment that works to cut crime."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside LIVE Updated 3 mins ago Droylsden explosives arrests LIVE as residents evacuated after bomb squad response Police said 'ammunition and potentially hazardous substances' were uncovered at a house in Droylsden The police scene in place in Droyl A major emergency services response descended on Shelley Grove in Droylsden on Wednesday afternoon (November 18), with police, fire and ambulance crews all in attendance. Bomb disposal experts were also called to the scene following the discovery at the property A cordon was put in place and residents were evacuated from their homes. Greater Manchester Police said officers attended the address at 2.22pm to make an arrest attempt as part of an ongoing and unrelated investigation A force spokesperson said: "Emergency services attended the scene, and officers recovered ammunition and discovered potentially hazardous substances. There is a cordon in place while the EOD (Explosive Ordnance Disposal) assesses the situation." Officers said a man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of criminal damage, arson, and possession of ammunition. A man in his 70s and a woman in her 60s have been arrested on suspicion of unlawfully possessing ammunition and explosive substances, GMP said In a post on the GMP Tameside Facebook page last night, police said the evacuation of the street was likely to remain in place today (Thursday). "As a precaution, residents on the affected street have been evacuated while emergency services continue their work", the post said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The secrets that led to the downfall of five prison officers The Prison Service in England and Wales have developed a scheme given to trainees to help them avoid being manipulated into illicit relationships by experienced criminals Top row, lef Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:01, 19 Nov 2026 Updated 07:42, 19 Nov 2026 It's a position held in the highest regard with the intense responsibility of guarding the most violent in our society. With that responsibility comes great scrutiny However, for some, temptation proved too much. In March 2026, the Ministry of Justice stated that between 2020 and 2025, 41 prison officers had been convicted of an offence of misconduct in a public office , where the offence related to an inappropriate relationship with a prison The Prison Service has since developed a scheme, the Enable programme, which designed to assist trainees with professional practice, capability and strengthening learning It is currently piloting a regional delivery model across London prisons and testing the model in Early Adopter sites, the service said. A redesigned Foundation Training programme for new prison officers is also being developed, with testing due to begin in 2027 A Prison Service spokesperson said: “Prison officers are the backbone of our service, working every day in some of the toughest conditions. That is why getting training right is essential to delivering punishment that works to cut crime."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The secrets that led to the downfall of five prison officers The Prison Service in England and Wales have developed a scheme given to trainees to help them avoid being manipulated into illicit relationships by experienced criminals Top row, lef Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:01, 19 Nov 2026 Updated 07:42, 19 Nov 2026 It's a position held in the highest regard with the intense responsibility of guarding the most violent in our society. With that responsibility comes great scrutiny However, for some, temptation proved too much. In March 2026, the Ministry of Justice stated that between 2020 and 2025, 41 prison officers had been convicted of an offence of misconduct in a public office , where the offence related to an inappropriate relationship with a prison The Prison Service has since developed a scheme, the Enable programme, which designed to assist trainees with professional practice, capability and strengthening learning It is currently piloting a regional delivery model across London prisons and testing the model in Early Adopter sites, the service said. A redesigned Foundation Training programme for new prison officers is also being developed, with testing due to begin in 2027 A Prison Service spokesperson said: “Prison officers are the backbone of our service, working every day in some of the toughest conditions. That is why getting training right is essential to delivering punishment that works to cut crime."

title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest

evidence_packet.title: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest
evidence_packet.lead: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move b
evidence_packet.summary: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move b
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017 Anna Morris KC, representing the Pearson family, said the ultimate culpability for the "heinous murders" was with the three perpetrators

title: Rochdale man who murdered wife and hid body under bed jailed

evidence_packet.title: Rochdale man who murdered wife and hid body under bed jailed
evidence_packet.lead: Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Howard was sentenced to a minimum of 21-and-a-half years in prison at Manche
evidence_packet.summary: Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Howard was sentenced to a minimum of 21-and-a-half years in prison at Manche
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Kyle Howard, 37, stabbed Keeley Aspinall, 44, to death in their Rochdale home on 23 May and hid her body under their bed for two days before alerting the authorities, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Howard was sentenced to a minimum of 21-and-a-half years in prison at Manchester Crown Court, after earlier pleading guilty to murder In a victim impact statement read to the court, Keeley's sister said: "I have never been so heartbroken in my life. I just wish I could have one more second with my sister." "I miss her so much and I'll never get to see her again," her sister said. "That was his choice to take her away "I have nightmares about what has happened to her - but I have found that being awake is worse than the actual nightmares I have at night." She said there was a "numbness, hurt and confusion", adding: "I feel Keeley's life is always going to be remembered by her murder - this is heartbreaking for us

evidence_packet.summary: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.lead: Cheers to the women who changed the way we drink!
evidence_packet.summary: Cheers to the women who changed the way we drink! Hear the hidden history of the female pioneers who drank, distilled, and defied , while enjoying cocktails inspired by them Drinking history expert Simon Sharp takes you on a journey from the invention of the pub and modern beer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheers to the women who changed the way we drink! Hear the hidden history of the female pioneers who drank, distilled, and defied , while enjoying cocktails inspired by them Drinking history expert Simon Sharp takes you on a journey from the invention of the pub and modern beer, to distillation and champagne – where women have been at the forefront , challenging patriarchy so we can all enjoy a drink To illustrate these stories guests will enjoy four cocktails; The Mansplainer, The Poinsettia, Bees Knees, and Hanky Panky – all invented or inspired by these trailblazing ladies, crafted with ingredients sourced from female founded and led businesses A tribute to women’s creativity and courage , this tasting celebrates the mark they’ve left on drinking culture Simon Sharp is a history geek, drinks expert, and spirits judge. He travels around the country hosting tastings and talks revolving around the history of drinking. He has also appeared on radio, podcasts, and newspapers expressing his enthusiasm for drinking history and culture Are you more independent or community focused? Experimental or measured? In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

The Inspiral Carpets man was right in the middle of Madchester and he’s still at it, touring and recently publishing his book, The Manchester Chronicles . He’ll be sharing the decks with DJ, presenter and podcaster Matt There’ll be a talk from John Barratt, co-founder of the Stockport Music Story with his wife Rosemary. evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

The title is the Latin plural of “asylum”, which can mean both a place of refuge and an institution for the insane – and the piece plays on this plurality. Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. Hailed by the LA Times as “an outright sensation”, Smith writes music drawn from field recordings and underwater microphones, looking for what she c The evening closes with Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite , one of the happiest accidents in musical history. Sergei Diaghilev, head of the Ballets Russes, saw his first three choices to score a new ballet fall through before he gambled on an unproven 27-year-old; Stravinsky himself la Four works, then, that each began as a risk on someone (to varying degrees) untested – Stravinsky in 1910, Adès in 1996, Smith tonight. If this is Adès’s opening statement as Principal Guest Conductor, it’s a heartening one: a little faith in emerging composers can go a long way

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Mauricio Pochettino immediately sends 20-word message to Man City that Man United fans will love Mauricio Pochettino has immediately been drawn into the Manchester derby rivalry as he prepares to take charge of United Add to preferred sources C Mauricio Pochettino gave a pointed 20-word message to Man City and insisted that, with time, he will make Manchester red again. Pochettino took charge of his final United States game on Tuesday before flying to the UK to start life as United boss The US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati to wrap up an 8-0 aggregate victory in their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Food & Drink Etihad Stadium New vibrant food hall to open by Etihad for Man City matchdays and gigs at Co-op Live Brickworks Market Hall, the latest destination to open at Medlock Square, and is bringing together some of Manchester’s best-loved independent operators und A brand new food and drink destination has opened between the Etihad Stadium and Co-op Live, as part of the expansion of Medlock Square. The £300m year-round entertainment, dining and cultural destination at Etihad Campus opened earlier this year with a new string of restaurants, The latest is Brickworks Market Hall, which is bringing together some of Manchester’s best-known independent operators under one roof. It features a wide mix of food offerings and two brand new bars Situated on the main square, fronting onto both the Etihad Stadium and Co-op Live, Brickworks Market Hall is currently open pre-and-post Etihad Stadium match days and Co-op Live events. Its food line up spans pizzas, Japanese street food, burgers, fried chicken and pies, as well Spanning 357sqm with capacity for 238 covers, Brickworks has been designed as a 'vibrant, bustling space' where flavours and concepts collide. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он прио 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне!
